source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: The lecture argued that the best person to write a skill is someone who is an expert in it. In the context of this assignment, why does that fit?

options.text: Because only an expert is permitted to edit a working skill's instructions
options.feedback: There is no restriction on who may edit a skill. The point is about the quality of judgment behind the edit, not about permission to make it.

options.text: Because you are the expert on what you want from the notes, and can say so precisely
options.feedback: A skill is only as good as the judgment written into its instructions. A student who knows what makes notes useful to them can state that directly, where an outsider can only guess at it.

options.text: Because a skill written by an expert never needs to be revised afterward
options.feedback: Skill Creator's own loop of test cases and judged output assumes skills keep getting revised. Expertise makes a better first draft, not a permanent one.

options.text: Because expertise is needed to operate the coding agent that edits a skill file
options.feedback: Running a coding-capable agent takes no subject-matter expertise, and a purely instructional skill needs no coding agent at all, as the earlier discussion of writing skills in chat established.
